propositions: An observer (consumer) of a user secret gets secret-changed when a new revision is published
An observer of a user secret gets no other secret hook (rotate/expired/remove are owner-scoped)
note: Uniter resolver fires secret-changed for ConsumedSecretInfo (internal/worker/uniter/secrets/resolver.go:71); rotate, expiry and obsolete watchers are filtered by CharmSecretOwner (secrets.go:806,859,930), so a model-owned user secret never drives those hooks in a consumer.

propositions: The vault backend config has a token key
token is optional in the schema but is the only Vault auth credential Juju passes, so normally it is set
note: token is Secret but not Mandatory (only endpoint is Mandatory, config.go:30-34). Juju authenticates only via vault.WithAuthToken (provider.go:371); client-cert/client-key configure TLS only, with no cert-auth login.

propositions: The vault secret backend type talks to HashiCorp Vault
note: BackendType = "vault"; the package imports github.com/hashicorp/vault/api (backend.go:10, provider.go:14) through mittwald/vaultgo.

propositions: Every relation, including a peer relation, has application databags (per endpoint) and unit databags (per relation unit) stored in the model database
Peer relations are created automatically for an application, so charms can use their databags to persist data
note: relation_application_setting is keyed by relation_endpoint_uuid and relation_unit_setting (line 144) by relation_unit_uuid; peer relations are inserted at application creation (domain/application/state/peer_relation.go:55). The 'charm authors use this' part is motivation and not testable. Unit settings are archived/removed when a unit leaves scope, so persistence is bounded by the relation/unit lifetime.

propositions: Any unit of the local application can read the remote application's application databag
Any local unit can read the remote units' databags
note: readOneRemoteSettings checks only that the caller is the local unit, then returns remote unit settings (uniter.go:2004) or remote application settings (2013) with no leadership check. Leadership gating applies only to reading/writing the local application databag (uniter.go ~1882-1906).

propositions: Secret names are validated against a pattern requiring a lowercase start, letters/digits/dashes, no trailing dash
The regex is ^(a-z{2,})$
correction: Juju applies no format check to user-secret names beyond non-empty and unique within the model; the regex ^([a-z](?:-?[a-z0-9]){2,})$ applies to secret content keys (min 3 chars, lowercase letters and digits, single dashes, no leading or trailing dash).
note: keyRegExp is used only on content keys (createsecret.go:110). add-secret takes args[0] as the name without validation (cmd/juju/secrets/add.go:89); the state layer only rejects an empty label (domain/secret/state/state.go:2109) and duplicates (SecretLabelAlreadyExists, domain/secret/errors/errors.go:22). The quoted regex is also mangled markdown: ^(a-z{2,})$ is not the real pattern and the key pattern allows digits but not uppercase.

propositions: A charm can grant a secret to another application in the context of a relation
Access is tied to the relation and removed with it
note: secret-grant requires a relation id (no relation -> error) and the grant is scoped to that relation (help text lines 44-45). The URI itself is passed through relation data. 'A database's address' is loose as an example of a secret but not refuted.

propositions: (Garbled: 'would not be insecure' must mean 'would be insecure') Configuring a vault backend with just endpoint and token does not establish an encrypted TLS connection
correction: Whether the connection to Vault uses TLS depends on the endpoint scheme (https); ca-cert (with optional client-cert/client-key and tls-server-name) supplies the CA used to verify the server, and is needed when Vault's certificate is not trusted by the system roots.
note: Juju always builds a TLSConfig from ca-cert/client-cert/client-key/tls-server-name and passes the endpoint to vault.NewClient; the hashicorp api client uses TLS for https URLs with system roots when CACertBytes is empty. So endpoint+token over https is encrypted; over http it is not. The sentence also has a typo inverting its meaning.

propositions: In the consuming model, the remote application is named after the SAAS name, which is the --alias given to consume or else the offer name
note: applicationName = arg.ApplicationAlias, defaulting to offerURL.Name (lines 1629-1638), then saveRemoteApplicationOfferer. Sentence is a fragment ending in 'e.g.' and has a grammar slip ('names is').

propositions: User secrets have no rotation policy, so no secret-rotate
User secrets have no expiry, so no secret-expired
Obsolete user-secret revisions are pruned by Juju, with no secret-remove hook
note: add-secret/update-secret expose only --info, --file, --name, --auto-prune (cmd/juju/secrets/common.go:24-25, update.go:112-113), no rotate/expire. Rotation/expiry/obsolete watchers take CharmSecretOwner only (watcher.go:178,410,448); user-secret pruning is a controller worker (WatchObsoleteUserSecretsToPrune, watcher.go:486).

propositions: juju machines prints columns Machine State Address Inst id Base AZ Message
Deploy prints 'Located charm ... in charm-hub, revision N' and 'Deploying ... from charm-hub charm ..., revision N in channel C on <base>'
LXD provisioning messages include 'Creating container', 'Container started', 'acquiring LXD image'
note: Deploy text formats at cmd/juju/application/deployer/charm.go:244 and :470; status messages at internal/provider/lxd/environ_broker.go:139,152 and internal/container/lxd/image.go:57. Defects are presentational: two code blocks are fused (stray 'text' token), a shell prompt 'ubuntu@charm-dev:~/.local/share/juju$' leaks in, and the trailing backtick after 'acquiring LXD image'.

propositions: A charm secret is owned by a charm entity (an application or a unit), as opposed to a user (model-owned) secret
note: CharmSecretOwnerKind is application or unit (types.go:217-222). More precisely, a charm secret is owned by the application or unit whose charm created it; ownership is the defining property.

propositions: Cross-model relations can join applications in models on different clouds/controllers (e.g. a machine cloud and Kubernetes)
note: Consuming an offer can record an external controller (saveExternalController), so the offering model can be on another controller and cloud. The I/O and density benefits are motivation, not testable.

propositions: Peer relations are the mechanism behind high availability of multi-unit applications
correction: Peer relations give an application's units a shared channel (databags and relation hooks) to coordinate, which charms can use to implement clustering or high availability; Juju itself attaches no HA behaviour to them.
note: In the code a peer relation is an ordinary relation auto-created from the charm's peers endpoints; no HA logic keys off it. HA is charm-implemented (and controller HA is separate).
